name: Multimodal Toxic Chinese Benchmark
description: Detecting toxic content using language models is important but challenging. While large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong performance in understanding Chinese, recent studies show that simple character substitutions in toxic Chinese text can easily confuse the state-of-the-art (SOTA) LLMs. In this paper, we highlight the multimodal nature of Chinese language as a key challenge for deploying LLMs in toxic Chinese detection. First, we propose a taxonomy of 3 perturbation strategies and 8 specific approaches in toxic Chinese content. Then, we curate a dataset based on this taxonomy, and benchmark 9 SOTA LLMs (from both the US and China) to assess if they can detect perturbed toxic Chinese text. Additionally, we explore cost-effective enhancement solutions like in-context learning (ICL) and supervised fine-tuning (SFT). Our results reveal two important findings. (1) LLMs are less capable of detecting perturbed multimodal Chinese toxic contents. (2) ICL or SFT with a small number of perturbed examples may cause the LLMs "overcorrect'': misidentify many normal Chinese contents as toxic.
reputation: Paper-proposed benchmark focused on Chinese toxic content perturbations; of interest to researchers in content moderation for Chinese but not yet widely adopted as a standard.
notes: Adversarial/perturbed inputs create distribution shift; small or targeted dataset portions may cause overfitting with few-shot or fine-tuning. Multimodal/character-level perturbations increase contamination risk for models trained on web data; caution needed when interpreting improvements from ICL or SFT due to potential 'overcorrection' effects.
